sources.entry: Scientific Writing Skills by David Sosa-Trejo - Six Agent Skills for scientific writing based on Stanford's Writing in the Sciences course: sentence-level prose editing, IMRaD manuscript structure, the writing process, peer review and publication, grants and recommendation letters, and lay summaries and press. Ships as the sciwrite Claude Code plugin with four stdlib-only Python audit scripts.

summary.one_liner: A set of six Claude agent skills plus four stdlib-only Python audit scripts that help researchers edit scientific prose, structure IMRaD manuscripts, run the writing process, handle peer review and publication, draft grants and letters, and write lay summaries.
summary.what_it_does: The repository packages instructions distilled from Stanford's "Writing in the Sciences" course into six skills: sciwrite-prose (sentence and paragraph editing), sciwrite-manuscript (IMRaD structure, tables and figures, verb tense per section), sciwrite-process (pre-writing, drafting, revision, pre-submission checklist), sciwrite-publish (journal choice, responding to reviewers, peer review, authorship, predatory journals), sciwrite-proposals (review articles, specific aims, research plans, recommendation letters, personal statements), and sciwrite-outreach (lay summaries, press interviews, risk communication, social media). Four Python scripts in the sciwrite-prose skill flag candidate issues: prose_audit.py checks dead-weight phrases, passive voice, to-be density, nominalisations and similar patterns; keyword_consistency.py finds terminology drift and acronyms used across sections; numeric_consistency.py checks sample sizes, abstract-to-body numbers and precision; extract_text.py pulls text and a section map from .tex, .docx, .md and .txt files. All scripts support JSON output and report candidates rather than verdicts. The README includes a before/after example showing a reduced word count and fewer flagged defects.
use_cases: editing a research paper for clarity and concision
checking a thesis chapter or manuscript section for weak prose
preparing a response to peer reviewers
drafting a grant specific aims page
writing a lay summary or press-friendly explanation of research
notable: Skills are derived from all eight units of Stanford's Writing in the Sciences course, with each rule citing its course module
Audit scripts use only the Python standard library and report candidates rather than verdicts
Supports LaTeX, Word, Markdown and plain text manuscripts, with section-level review
Includes a second set of engineering and computer vision examples alongside the biomedical ones from the course
Skills load detailed reference files only when a task needs them
caveats: Not a content reviewer; it improves how claims are delivered and does not check scientific correctness
Not affiliated with Stanford or Kristin Sainani; the course itself is copyrighted and not redistributed
Scripts flag false positives by design, such as passive voice in Methods or repeated keywords
